'''Ekelarc Yong''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served as a [[lieutenant]] and [[starfighter]] [[pilot]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. He flew a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]] under the [[callsign]] [[Gray Three]] as a member of [[Gray Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gray Squadron]] and participated in the [[Battle of Endor]], in which the Alliance aimed to destroy the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]].

After realizing they had fallen into a trap, the rebels engaged with an [[Imperial Navy|Imperial fleet]] at point blank range in order to avoid being targeted by the [[Death Star]]'s [[superlaser]]. During the fighting, Yong's [[bomber]] was shot down by two [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s, although the [[pilot]] managed to crash the vehicle into the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of an Imperial [[Star Destroyer]] as he [[Death|died]].

==Biography==
[[Lieutenant]]<ref name="SWCT">{{SWCT|set=2021 Base - Series 3|cardname=Lt. Ekelarc Yong}}</ref> Ekelarc Yong<ref name="Rebel Pilots Databank" /> was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]], flying as a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]] [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] in the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] of the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]]. When the [[fleet]] jumped<ref name="Episode VI" /> from the [[Sullust system]]<ref name="RotJ novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref> to the [[Endor system]] in order to [[Battle of Endor|attack]] the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]]<ref name="Episode VI" /> in [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Death" /> Yong flew with them under the [[callsign]] [[Gray Three]] in [[Gray Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gray Squadron]],<ref name="Rebel Pilots Databank" /> a mixed [[starfighter]] [[squadron]] of [[BTL Y-wing starfighter|Y-wings]], [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter]]s, and [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]]s<ref name="SWGeek">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref> commanded by [[Gray Leader]] [[Horton Salm]].<ref name="RSOWM">''[[Rebel Starfighters Owners' Workshop Manual]]''</ref>

The Alliance believed that the Empire was unaware of its attack plans and that the unfinished [[Death Star]]'s [[Deflector shield|shields]] would be down; however, upon arriving in the [[Endor]] [[Star system|system]], [[General]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] quickly realized they had walked into a trap and called off the first attack run. An [[Imperial Navy|Imperial fleet]] then engaged the Alliance,<ref name="Episode VI" /> with hundreds<ref name="RotJ novel" /> of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]]s and [[TIE/IN interceptor]]s swarming the rebel starfighters. The fleet then held out against the [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]] while waiting for a [[Endor strike team|strike team]] they had sent to the [[moon]] of [[Endor]] to disabled the [[Death Star's shield generator]].<ref name="Episode VI" />

When the Death Star revealed that its [[superlaser]] was functional by destroying the [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser|MC80 ''Liberty'' Type Heavy Star Cruiser]] ''[[Liberty]]'', Calrissian ordered the Alliance's forces to engaged the Imperial [[Star Destroyer]]s they were facing at point blank range<ref name="Episode VI" /> so that the Death Star could not fire upon them.<ref name="RotJ novel" /> Yong then flew in tight along the side of one of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]] with two TIE fighters on his tail, but his [[bomber]] was struck by fire from the pursuers<ref name="Episode VI" /> and began to spin out of control. Making the most of a bad situation, Yong managed to crash his vehicle into the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of another Star Destroyer,<ref name="Rebel Pilots Databank" /> [[Death|perishing]] in the blast.<ref name="Death" />

==Personality and traits==
Yong had dark [[hair]], dark [[eye]]s, and light skin.<ref name="Episode VI" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Ekelarc_Yong_Y-wing_Helmet_ROTJ.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Yong's [[flight helmet]]]]
Ekelarc Yong first appeared in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="Episode VI" /> The Y-wing cockpit scenes for ''Return of the Jedi'' were filmed on Stage 9 at [[Elstree Studios]] between [[March 2]] and [[March 11]], [[1982]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> The character's chest pack featured the joke inscription "HELP HELD CAPTIVE AT ILM."<ref name="Costumes">''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref>

In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the character was first identified in [[2014]] in the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]], although the website erroneously uses an image of [[Gureni Telsij]], another Y-wing pilot, instead of Yong.<ref name="Rebel Pilots Databank" /> A card released in [[2021]] on the ''[[Star Wars: Card Trader]]'' app also makes this error.<ref name="SWCT" /> The character's name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used on a "Battle Over Endor" action figure set produced by [[Hasbro]] in [[2010]].<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Dark Side|pack=(Toys R Us Exclusive) Battle Over Endor (1 of 2)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TVCEXBattleOverEndor1.asp}}</ref> A 2014 news article detailed how [[Leland Chee]] was consulted due to the actor's Asian ethnicity but the actor was not clearly identified.<ref name="NPR">{{WebCite|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/codeswitch/2014/12/29/372670957/diversity-in-space-tracking-the-first-asian-pilot-in-the-star-wars-movies|text=Diversity In Space: Tracking The First Asian Pilot In The Star Wars Movies|author=Haruch, Steve|date=2014-12-14|work=[[Wikipedia:National Public Radio|National Public Radio]]|archivedate=20190518192028}}</ref> The article also mentioned how the actor might also be the same as [[Gureni Telsij]].
